name: two_tank_sequence
description: Two-tank fill/transfer/drain demonstrator: TK-101 is filled through XV-101, transferred to TK-102 through XV-102 and drained through XV-103, sequenced by PLC-101 from LT-101/LT-102 levels and START/STOP/SHUT pushbuttons. Hand-written golden IR from the L1 bundle with the CR-004 effective parameter set.

Command XV-101 open. XV-102 and XV-103 closed. Transition when LT-101 >= T1_High.
V1 closed; V2 and V3 commanded open together. Remain in SHUTDOWN until both tanks are at or below their low-level limits, then close all valves and go to IDLE.
SHUT has the highest command priority. A valid SHUT edge immediately abandons any stored resume context and enters SHUTDOWN.
START has the lowest priority. START from IDLE begins FILL_T1; START from PAUSED restores the interrupted state. START while already running is ignored.
When STOP occurs in WAIT_AFTER_FILL, WAIT_AFTER_TRANSFER or WAIT_AFTER_DRAIN, the remaining delay shall be retained. START shall resume with that remaining delay.
Level threshold comparisons shall include equality (>= high, <= low).

Legacy simulation code uses states FILL, HOLD1, TRANSFER, HOLD2, DRAIN and HOLD3. These map to FILL_T1, WAIT_AFTER_FILL, TRANSFER_T1_T2, WAIT_AFTER_TRANSFER, DRAIN_T2 and WAIT_AFTER_DRAIN respectively.
**D-01:** Command precedence is `SHUT > STOP > START`.
**D-03:** STOP during any delay freezes the remaining delay; START resumes the remaining delay.
**D-05:** START and STOP received during active SHUT are ignored.
**D-06:** SHUT is complete only when both LT-101 and LT-102 are at or below their low-level setpoints.
type StepState = enumeration(IDLE,FILL,HOLD1,TRANSFER,HOLD2,DRAIN,HOLD3);

assumptions.text: Each valve passes its constant nominal flow when commanded open and none when closed, independent of tank level; valve stroke time is neglected.

trace.quote: For the hackathon simulation the dynamic valve stroke is neglected and each valve is treated as an ideal Boolean flow switch.

assumptions.text: No pulse width is given for the pushbuttons; each press is assumed to be true for one 1 s logging interval, as in the reference trace. Only its rising edge matters.
